prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Pick Your Companion Archetype", "Select a starter pet style to get up and running instantly."]
1: ["What Kind of Pet Companion Do You Want?", "Choose a desktop buddy tailored for productivity, relaxation, or fun."]
2: ["Signing in anchors your pet to your cloud account so your pet's state and memory are safe."]
3: ["Tuning Your Pet's Desktop Behavior", "Adjust companion activity levels while your pet finishes loading."]
4: ["Welcome Your Companion to the Desktop!", "Here is how to interact with your pet: right-click for options, drag to move, double-click to chat."]
5: ["Save & Protect Your Companion", "Create or log into your account so your pet companion stays saved across sessions."]
6: ["Review your companion details before completing adoption."]
7: ["Tip: You can hide or call your pet anytime using your system tray or double-clicking its icon."]
8: ["Preparing your desktop companion environment..."]
9: ["Choose Your Desk Companion Type", "Select whether you want an active interactive friend or a calm background presence."]
